messages:
maya: Heads up — hitting a weird failure when onboarding the new quantized-4bit LlamaX. Tool/function detection is not triggering on any of the tool-tag examples in our eval harness.
leo: do you mean JSON mode payloads aren't parsed by the runtime?
maya: yeah. The HF model conversion added `additional_special_tokens` but tokenizer still splits the <tool> tag across tokens after quantization. So our JSON mode sentinel gets fragmented and the parser misses it.
olivia: ugh that fragmentation is brutal with 4bit quantized vocab alignments. Did you check tokenizer.add_special_tokens vs special_tokens_map? They behave differently in hf.
maya: tried both. added_tokens gets recognized by hf tokenizers, but the exported tokenizer.json in the converted model ends up with byte-level merges that break exact string match.
samir: quick idea — use a short sentinel token that is a single unicode codepoint (rare char) and register it as a single special token before quantization. e.g. "\uE000" range private use. That avoids subword split.
leo: good call. Also make sure config.json has "add_bos_token": false/true matching our chat template. Mismatched role tokens cause the assistant/role anchors to shift and then the tool call walker fails.
maya: noted. For posterity here are the minimal checks I ran:
```
# tokenizer sanity
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("./converted-llamax")
print(t.encode("<RW_TOOL_START>{\"name\":\"search\"}\n"))
print(t.convert_ids_to_tokens(t.encode("<RW_TOOL_START>{\"name\":\"search\"}")))
```
If the tokenized output shows multiple tokens for `<RW_TOOL_START>` we get problems.
olivia: also watch for role tokens like "<|assistant|>" vs our internal "<assistant>". HF chat templates sometimes insert whitespace or BOS/EOS that shift token indexes.
samir: for a robust rollout: (1) pick private-use sentinel single-codepoint, (2) add into tokenizer special tokens BEFORE merging/quantization, (3) bake mapping in conversion script so tokenizer.json contains the exact token string, (4) add unit test that `tokenizer.decode(tokenizer.encode(sentinel)) == sentinel`.
maya: implemented 1–3 locally. CI unit test failing on CI quantize job — looks like the quantization tool (qat-optimizer) reorders vocab and collapses private-use to multi-bytes?
leo: we should file an infra ticket but also add a fallback in parser: if sentinel not found, try heuristic fix — look for sequences that match known splits and reassemble into the tool tag. not ideal but reduces regressions.
olivia: +1 for fallback in parser. But please log when fallback used and surface in Optimize/Console regression alerts. We need to detect if fallback changes token boundaries for cost estimates.
samir: infra-bot can we trigger the quantize job with the latest tokenizer patch?
infra-bot: deploy: triggered quantize-job/llamax-4bit with patch branch maya/tool-sentinel-ux — job 983274 started.
maya: thanks. I'll add the parser fallback and the token reassembly test in the eval harness. will post results once CI finishes. :thumbsup:
leo: if CI passes, next step is a small perf/quality sweep comparing original vs quantized for tool-calling recall. benchmark script: run 5k tool-call prompts, measure true positive detection rate and token overhead.
maya: will run that and share numbers.
